news.headline: WTI Crude Oil -1.61% to $93.09 on US-Iran Hormuz Deal Hopes
news.what_happened: WTI crude fell to $93.09/bbl (-1.61%) as reports emerged of US-Iran negotiations aimed at restoring Persian Gulf exports. Only 10 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday vs the 10-day average of 17, but diplomatic signals drove crude lower. Brent also fell -0.76% to $105.79.
news.why_it_matters: A $1/bbl crude drop saves India ~8,000-10,000 Cr/year on import bill and directly reduces costs for aviation (jet fuel 35-40% of OPEX), tyres (crude derivatives 60-70% input cost), paints (petrochemical feedstock 40-50% of raw materials) and logistics companies. Negative for OMCs and upstream oil producers.

news.headline: US 10Y Treasury Yield Spikes to 5.162% — Near Post-2004 High
news.what_happened: US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.162% (+0.94%) while the 30-year yield touched a post-2004 peak of 5.438%. The surge reflects higher-for-longer Fed rate expectations and rising fiscal concerns. Indian 10Y G-Sec also rose 6bps to 7.11%, highest since May 21.
news.why_it_matters: Surging US yields drive FII outflows from emerging markets. India saw FII sell net 5,027 Cr on Sep 24. Continued yield pressure = sustained selling in Nifty 50 blue chips. Domestic yield rise is directly bearish for real estate, NBFCs and rate-sensitive sectors.

news.headline: FII Net Sell 5,027 Cr on Sep 24 — Largest Single-Day Outflow in Weeks
news.what_happened: Foreign institutional investors were aggressive net sellers of 5,027.40 Cr in cash markets on Sep 24, while simultaneously holding a net short index-futures position of 3,09,822 contracts. DII stepped in buying 4,301.20 Cr, providing partial buffer. Nifty 50 fell -1.64%.
news.why_it_matters: FIIs hold 40%+ of free-float in Nifty 50 companies. Heavy selling + net short futures = institutional bears are in control. With US 10Y at 5.16%, FII outflows may persist in near term. Stocks with highest FII ownership face most pressure.

news.headline: Nikkei +1.24%, Hang Seng -1.51% — Asia Divided on Trump-Xi Talks
news.what_happened: Japan's Nikkei surged 1.24% to 66,326 on optimism around US-China trade talks. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.51% to 24,387 as China mainland markets remained closed and Yuan weakened 21 pips to 6.7489. Mixed signals on Trump-Xi meeting outcome.
news.why_it_matters: China mainland closure and Hang Seng weakness are bearish for Indian metals (China is the biggest buyer of steel, aluminium). Nikkei strength provides some positive risk-on overlay but insufficient to offset China risk-off.

news.headline: Natural Gas -3.29% to $3.259 — Fertilizer Feedstock Cost Tailwind
news.what_happened: Natural gas futures fell 3.29% to $3.259/mmBtu on mild weather forecasts and rising US storage inventory data. Sharpest single-day fall in weeks.
news.why_it_matters: Natural gas is the primary feedstock for urea and ammonia (fertilizer) production. A 3%+ decline directly expands EBITDA margins for domestic fertilizer producers. Also marginally positive for gas-based power plants.

picks.catalyst: WTI Crude Oil -1.61% to $93.09 on US-Iran Hormuz deal progress
picks.logic: Jet fuel is 35-40% of IndiGo's OPEX. Every $1/bbl crude drop saves approximately 350-400 Cr/year. With WTI now at $93, cost trajectory is meaningfully improving. Stock fell -2.75% on Sep 24 due to broad market selloff (not IndiGo-specific), making the crude catalyst even more compelling at current depressed levels. R:R 2.45x.

picks.catalyst: Gold +0.61% to $4,324/oz; risk-off environment sustains gold demand
picks.logic: Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold loan NBFC. Gold rising 0.61% expands per-gram loan disbursement limits and improves collateral coverage on existing loans. Risk-off environment (surging US yields, FII selling) is supportive for gold as a safe haven. Short-tenor gold loan book (90-180 days) insulates from duration risk vs rate-sensitive peers. R:R 2.17x.
